findings.text: cpuset_write_resmask is an externally visible store operation for cpuset resource list controls. It rejects use on the top set, normalizes caller text, requires online status, validates against a trial copy, and reports an error or the accepted length.

cpuset_common_seq_show is an externally visible display operation shared by multiple cpuset list controls. It resolves the enclosing set and a file discriminator and renders the matching configured or effective processor or memory view.

cpuset_init establishes initial state for the top set and global processor tracking at boot. It creates fully permissive processor and memory allowances for the root, prepares attach scratch state and legacy state, and derives initial isolated processors from boot housekeeping configuration when enabled.

cpuset_cgrp_subsys publishes cpuset controller callbacks and file tables to the cgroup layer. It advertises set allocation and lifecycle handling, task attach and fork handling, hierarchy binding, default and optional legacy controls, early initialization, and threaded support.

Validation before moving tasks between sets. It collapses repeated destination checks for identical source and destination pairs, ignores tasks whose source already equals the destination in threaded cases, checks each distinct move and each task for eligibility, enforces scheduler permission when scheduling scope changes, accounts deadline tasks, rejects unsupported multi destination shapes, and reserves deadline bandwidth before allowing the move.

A shared attach context links validation with completion. Validation clears multiplicity and change indicators, selects a representative source with preference for a thread group leader, and otherwise retains the first distinct source. Success holds progress for completion while failure discards collected source and destination records.

Attach validation and cancellation serialize on cpuset_mutex. The mutex covers inspection of task collections, updates to shared attach state and deadline accounting, progress counting, and cleanup of collected records.

Per task completion of a validated move. It selects an allowed processor set suited to the destination with distinct top set handling, applies affinity, updates node mask and legacy spread state except for default hierarchy moves without memory change, and for leaders with memory change rebinds policy with conditional address space migration and deferred flush coordination.

Group completion for validated moves. It expects caller held processor protection, derives a guaranteed online node set, skips task work when nothing migrates, uses a fast path for default hierarchy enablement without effective change that only refreshes stored prior allowances, otherwise completes tasks individually, coordinates deferred migration flushing, records the new prior allowance, and releases collected state and progress.

Configured allowances, effective views, and stored prior memory allowances are distinct. Completion refreshes the stored prior allowance from the newly guaranteed online set. Default hierarchy moves without reported effective change leave task processor and memory state untouched.

Pending deadline migration counts are incremented in the destination and decremented in the source for each migrating deadline task. Additional bandwidth accumulation applies only to tasks needing a root domain move. A collective reservation after the scan can reject the entire migration.

Store dispatch for processor, exclusive processor, and memory list controls by file discriminator. It coordinates through top mutex with processor and attach protection, requires online status, evaluates on a duplicate, releases the duplicate, finishes with scheduler and housekeeping coordinated unlock, and defers memory migration work after memory stores.

Display dispatch across configured and effective processor and memory lists plus exclusive, effective exclusive, subpartition, and isolated processor views. It holds callback protection during dispatch and signals an error for unknown discriminators.

Partition role display covers member, root, isolated, invalid root, and invalid isolated, with invalid variants optionally including a stored diagnostic explanation. The store path accepts only member, root, and isolated names, rejects other text, and applies the transition under top and processor and attach coordination only when online.

Default hierarchy exposes controls named cpus, mems, cpus.effective, mems.effective, cpus.partition, cpus.exclusive, cpus.exclusive.effective, cpus.subpartitions, and cpus.isolated. The first two plus partition and exclusive controls are absent on the root, while subpartitions and isolated appear only on the root, with subpartitions marked for debug visibility. Partition store vocabulary is root, member, and isolated.

Observed set state includes configured processor and memory allowances, effective processor and memory views, exclusive and effective exclusive processor views, stored prior memory allowance, partition role and diagnostic code, scheduling and migration flags, pending deadline counts and bandwidth sums, subsystem linkage, partition file location, and attach linkage. Global state includes the top set, subpartition and isolated processor tracking, attach scratch mask, and shared attach context with source, change, multiplicity, progress, node set, and deferred work indicators.

Set lifecycle covers allocation, online transition, offline transition, killed notification, release, and hierarchy binding. Allocation returns the shared top state for the root and otherwise provides a fresh set with default scheduling, legacy, and default hierarchy migration behavior. Online attaches under the parent with reference and effective state setup. Offline and killed perform flag, partition, and reference cleanup. Binding establishes mode and top allowances for the active hierarchy.

A newly online non root set inherits effective processor and memory views from its parent under callback protection. In default hierarchy it clears CS_SCHED_LOAD_BALANCE when the parent lacks it, while allocation sets CS_SCHED_LOAD_BALANCE always and CS_MEMORY_MIGRATE for default hierarchy. Reference counting brackets the online interval with legacy handling under full protection.

Fork handling separates same set continuation from cross set creation. Same set cases complete early or propagate processor and memory allowances directly. Cross set cases validate the destination and the new task, enforce scheduler permission, hold attach progress, and complete with memory guarantee, prior allowance recording, per task handling, deferred flush, and progress release.

Cross set fork validation requires caller held cgroup protection and serializes additionally on cpuset_mutex. Same set detection uses read side protection for comparing current and target sets. Cancellation and completion balance the progress hold.

Hotplug reconciliation for a single set substitutes parent effective views when computed processor or memory results are empty, except that a valid partition root may retain an empty processor result. It then publishes effective views under callback protection and propagates processor changes to task affinities and memory changes to task node masks.

Hotplug entry for a set recomputes effective processor and memory candidates under attach coordination, applies partition specific adjustments including remote handling and possible invalidation or revalidation with scheduler rebuild, skips further work when effective state is unchanged, validates memory configuration on memory change, and dispatches to hierarchy specific propagation before releasing protection.

Hotplug partition transitions move a local valid partition to invalid when its parent is invalid, grants no processors to children, or lacks subpartition grants, and move an invalid partition toward update when its parent is valid and exclusive effective state is non empty. A remote partition records a hotplug diagnostic and disables itself when subpartition grants vanish or when populated yet empty.

List displays hold callback_lock with interrupt exclusion. Online, offline, and killed paths use full cpuset protection, while binding combines cpuset_mutex with callback_lock. Resource and partition stores combine cpuset_top_mutex with processor read protection and attach completion coordination, ending with scheduler and housekeeping coordinated unlock. Processor protection and cpuset lock holding are asserted in attach paths.

Validation warns once and rejects multiple destinations combined with non default hierarchy or reported processor or memory changes. Per task affinity application is expected to succeed after validation and warns once otherwise. Missing representative source during completion is treated as highly unlikely with task work skipped. Boot allocation failures are fatal.

Policy rebinding and page migration apply only to thread group leaders when memory change was reported, with migration further gated by per set migrate behavior. Other tasks and moves without memory change stop after affinity and node handling. Successful migration uses the representative source allowance as origin and coordinates deferred flushing.
